articles.title_orig: Iran has a 2-day plan to reopen strait, resume nuclear talks with US, and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: Iran has a 2-day plan to reopen strait, resume nuclear talks with US, and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
Another vessel was struck by an "unknown projectile" near the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report Monday by the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center, or UKTMO, a maritime security agency.
The strike happened Sunday in an area about nine nautical miles off the coast of Lima, Oman, UKTMO said. It caused a hole to form on the starboard side of the vessel, although all crew members were reported safe by its captain, according to the agency.
"Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO, whilst authorities investigate," it said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections in the U.S., according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter, each of whom spoke with the Associated Press. Their comments followed an earlier report from Axios, which cited sources who said Netanyahu had pushed for President Trump to strike Iran during a call between the two leaders over the weekend, but Mr. Trump wanted to let the negotiations play out.
The two regional officials told AP that diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. Both officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the U.S. lifting its blockade on Iran's ports.
They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American, and in one case Israeli, officials.
One official said Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the U.S. administration to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.
Other U.S. allies in the Middle East are warning against more strikes, saying it would destabilize the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.
That official wasn't authorized to speak publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.
The Israeli government did not immediately comment. The White House did not directly respond to questions about Netanyahu and Trump's discussion of potential new strikes during the weekend call.
Iran's vice president said on Monday that exchanges with the U.S. via mediators indicated Washington's recognition of Tehran's "victory" in the Middle East war, Iranian state media reported.
"Our enemy failed to achieve any of its objectives in the last two wars. Even today, although the United States, driven by its own goals and concerns regarding domestic public opinion, is engaging in various maneuvers, the messages conveyed to Iran through intermediaries point to an acknowledgment of our victory," said Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref, according to IRNA state news agency.
Oil prices sank around seven percent on Monday, the eve of crucial midterm elections in the U.S., as signals that Tehran and Washington were renewing dialogue boosted hopes of ending the Middle East war.
Earlier, Axios outlet reported that Vice President JD Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, in the highest-level move from the Trump administration in months.
Arne Lohmann Rasmussen, chief analyst at Global Risk Management, told AFP that her organization believes such signals from the administration "may be tactical" ahead of the midterms.
"Meanwhile, attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continue [and] we maintain our higher-for-longer outlook for energy prices," Rasmussen said.
But share prices of energy majors have dropped, while many other sectors were boosted by the cooling fuel costs. Stocks got a lift from sharp drops in oil prices, which headed back down in their latest yo-yo move on uncertainty about when the war with Iran will allow the global industry to return to normal. The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, fell 7.4% to $105.03.
The price for the most actively traded contract in the Brent market has been veering between roughly $70 and $120 per barrel since just before the war began, and it's been quick to reverse direction.
Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, a military spokesperson for the Iran-backed Houthis, said Monday that the Saudi coalition fighting the rebel group in Yemen had launched more than 100 airstrikes over the course of the last day.
"Saudi warplanes launched 109 airstrikes over the past 24 hours," the spokesperson said in a statement shared on X. The strikes targeted the Yemeni provinces of Saada, Taiz, Lahj, Al-Jawf, and Hodeidah, according to the statement. Some of those provinces are in Houthi-controlled or contested territories.
The spokesperson said airstrikes between Sunday and Monday brought the total number of Saudi strikes and missile attacks to 3,939 since the fighting in Yemen escalated earlier this fall.
Saree's latest comments came after he claimed in another statement Monday that the Houthis had carried out new attacks against Saudi Arabian infrastructure, including a civilian airport, over the last 48 hours.
A spokesman for the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed Monday that the group had carried out new attacks over the preceding 48 hours on Saudi Arabian infrastructure, including a civilian airport.
Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, the Houthis' military spokesman, said in a statement shared on social media that the group had struck Saudi Arabia's eastern Dammam Airport  "using two drones, and the operation achieved its objective successfully, resulting in the disruption of air traffic at the airport."
He said another drone hit an "early warning radar in Jizan," a city on Saudi Arabia's western Red Sea coast, while unspecified Houthi weapons hit "a military transport aircraft at Jizan Airport."
The Houthis have peppered Saudi Arabia's airports and energy infrastructure for weeks in retaliation for the kingdom's backing of Yemen's government in the impoverished Middle Eastern nation's grueling decade-long civil war. Iran has long backed the Houthis as a powerful proxy force, particularly as a counter to Iran's arch-foe Saudi Arabia, which shares a long border with Yemen.
Houthi drone and missile strikes last month killed at least 20 people at Saudi airports , and despite the kingdom's vast military and financial advantage over the rebels, it has been unable to stop the attacks .
There was no immediate information from Saudi officials to confirm or deny Saree's claims on Monday.
The Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, had a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday, Iranian state media reported, in a continuation of recent talks between the two countries about the situation in the Middle East.
During their call, Rezaei and Putin discussed regional and global affairs, focusing on West Asia and ongoing "strategic cooperation" between Iran and Russia, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency.
Iran and Russia have long been allies, and their relationship has been cemented during both the ongoing Russian assault on Ukraine, and the U.S. war with Iran. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in October that Tehran's ties with Russia were closer than ever, contradicting Mr. Trump's assertion at the time that Moscow was "doing very little, if anything, to help" Tehran amid the war.
According to Tasnim, Rezaei thanked Putin Monday for Russia's support.
Iran's top diplomat said Monday that negotiations with the U.S., via mediators, aimed at reaching an agreement to end the war have been "proceeding very intensively," but he added that "everything depends on Washington's political rationality," according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.

articles.title_orig: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba comes to China in December
articles.title_zh: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba comes to China in December
articles.content_orig:
After many months of discussion , Apple has figured out a way to bring Apple Intelligence to China, working with Alibaba’s Qwen model on some features. Apple Intelligence will soon be made available as a developer beta and will ship to Chinese customers in December with iOS 27.3.
China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approved the use of Alibaba AI models with the iPhone in October 2026. Confirming the complexity of bringing these tools to China, Apple also received clearance in July from the Cyberspace Administration of China. Apple watchers are at liberty to reflect that the news comes at the best possible time for the company, which continues to grow smartphone market share in China.
The promise of integrated AI support in the form of Apple Intelligence can only boost interest in the company’s recently introduced iPhone Duo . Recent Counterpoint Research data claims iPhone sales increased 29% year on year in China in the three weeks following launch of the 18 Pro series devices. Initial stock of the devices sold out in hours.
China is also the world’s biggest market for foldable devices, which prompted some enterprising individuals to attempt to resell purchased iPhone Duos for far above their store price — scalpers have since reduced prices , because even in iPhone-crazy China, people weren’t willing to pay so much.
While it’s a big step for Apple AI in China, it’s not quite the great leap Apple may have wanted to put in place.
Siri AI is not supported and won’t be “anytime soon,” according to market speculation . While little is said about the reasons for that, it seems probable that political pressure in both the US and China may be partly to blame, as both nations see control of the means of AI production as essential for the future success of their differing ideologies. Apple has had to allow the Chinese government to approve ongoing updates to the suite.
Chinese users can use Alibaba’s Qwen in Siri, writing tools, and visual intelligence, including functions related to text and image understanding. They don’t get Image Playground, but can expect:
Apple and Alibaba also promise to maintain privacy. Customers will be able to choose if they wish to proceed with making a request through Qwen. Alibaba also said it would not use these requests for model training, though it isn’t yet clear if requests are going to Private Cloud Compute in Apple’s Chinese AI deployment.
Will the introduction of Apple Intelligence in China make a difference? It probably already is, as months of ever stronger speculation mean most Chinese consumers knew Apple AI was coming to their iPhones even as they purchased them before the announcement took place.
While the initial sales rush on Apple’s new devices among Chinese consumers has slowed, the news may help generate fresh enthusiasm for the iPhone in China. That’s great for Apple, but not such great news for some smaller smartphone vendors, who continue to be hammered by vicious increases in memory and other component prices.
Speaking almost two years ago when industry observers had anticipated an Apple Intelligence launch in China would take place earlier, Morgan Stanley then suggested the Alibaba partnership would be “a critical catalyst for Apple’s competitive standing in China.”
Other than painful price increases, not much has changed, and the introduction can only help consolidate the iPhone’s appeal in China. That’s good for Apple’s customers there, and great news for Apple’s investors everywhere else. It may even do something to retain a little US soft power.
In the background, we see the continued economic pressure wrought by fast-increasing memory prices. This has driven smartphone makers to raise prices, which has itself driven a 21% year on year decline in sector sales .
Apple and Samsung have proved more resilient to these price hikes than others, which means the added appeal generated by the launch of Apple Intelligence in the world’s second-largest economy is likely to make a highly significant difference to its market share in the short term, as well as shoring up share in future replacement cycles.
Now please subscribe to my daily, human-curated Apple-related news headline feed at The Core , or follow me on BlueSky , LinkedIn , or Mastodon .
Hello, and thanks for dropping in. I'm pleased to meet you. I'm Jonny Evans, and I've been writing (mainly about Apple) since 1999. These days I write my daily AppleHolic blog at Computerworld.com, where I explore Apple's growing identity in the enterprise. You can also keep up with my work at AppleMust , and follow me on BlueSky , Mastodon , and LinkedIn .

articles.title_orig: Russell Brand’s Defense Comes to a Close in His U.K. Rape Trial
articles.title_zh: Russell Brand’s Defense Comes to a Close in His U.K. Rape Trial
articles.content_orig:
Things you buy through our links may earn Vox Media a commission.
Russell Brand’s rape trial is coming to an end, and his defense team’s closing speech reiterated claims that “Brand is innocent.” The comedian’s barrister, Ian Winter KC, argued that that despite what he called mischaracterizations of his client in the media, Brand is not a psychopath and only a psychopath could have committed the behavior he is being accused of. “You would have to be a psychopath to be raping someone and asking them if they were enjoying it at the same time,” Winter said, referring to the first of Brand’s accusers, per Sky News . He then noted that Brand “left his actual email address — rapists do not leave their address. He left photos she’d taken of him, rapists do not leave their photographs; and he kissed her good-bye, or tried to, when he left.”
Brand is pleading not guilty to allegations from six women spanning a decade, from 1999 to 2009. He is facing one count of rape from 1999, one count of attempted indecent assault from 2001, one count each of oral rape and sexual assault from 2004, another count of sexual assault from between 2004 and 2005, and counts of both anal rape and sexual assault in 2009. That adds up to three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one charge of attempted indecent assault.
In Brand’s defense, Winter came out strongly against a 2023 Channel Four documentary about the comedian, in which five women accused him of “rape, sexual assaults, and emotional abuse.” Winter said the journalists involved with the documentary “poisoned the well of justice” by prompting other women to come forward with allegations. “They are all, we say, thoroughly contaminated by the program,” Winter claimed. “The very existence of them as complainants is fundamentally corrupted by that program and publicity and [that] renders it fundamentally unfair.” Speaking about a woman who says Brand attempted to drag her into a bathroom for sex while she resisted, for example, Winter claimed this was not criminal and she was only accusing Brand because she had been “poisoned” by the documentary. “He was behaving like a crazy lunatic,” Winter said. “But when she put her foot down and said, ‘No way,’ he accepted it.”

articles.title_orig: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman meetings
articles.title_zh: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman meetings
articles.content_orig:
China is stepping up its diplomatic efforts in the Middle East, including over the US-Israel war on Iran , following a lapse in activity.
Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Monday met a senior Iranian security official in Beijing, while President Xi Jinping hosted Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq for a landmark state visit.
Wang told Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, that dialogue and negotiation remained “the only viable path forward” as conflicts in the region “drag on and risk further spillover”.
He also reaffirmed China’s support for Iran’s sovereignty and security. Beijing has consistently blamed the US and Israel for starting the conflict.
“China is very close to Tehran; it is the biggest trading partner of Iran, the biggest customer of Iranian crude,” said Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Beijing.
However, Beijing’s diplomacy efforts have recently been stalled, she noted.
“It’s been a few weeks or even months [in which] China really hasn’t done much diplomatically towards … ending the war,” Yu said.
The meetings on Monday appear to illustrate that China is growing impatient with the lack of progress.
“I think China is very frustrated, and it wants to be seen to enter [the process],” Yu said.
Reflecting the step up in activity, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Monday that Zhai Jun, Beijing’s special envoy on the Middle East, will visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.
Meanwhile, Xi received Sultan Haitham, the first Omani head of state to visit China since the two countries established diplomatic relations in 1978.
The Chinese president said the Middle East and Gulf “should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict”.
Sitting across from Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, Oman is a key player in navigation on the strategic waterway, through which one-fifth of global energy exports traversed before the US-Iran war restricted traffic.
China is one of the world’s largest energy importers. Xi described bilateral ties with Oman as being at a “new historical starting point”.
During the visit, China and Oman signed 14 cooperation documents, covering areas including artificial intelligence, green energy and supply chains, along with a currency swap agreement.
In a joint statement, they called for safe navigation to resume through Hormuz and urged the US and Iran to restart dialogue.
Yu said the conflict had made the relationship “more of a priority for both sides”, particularly given the disruption to China’s energy imports.
“Oman is particularly important because many of its ports are outside the strait,” she said.

articles.title_zh: Cyberattacks hit supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe, Belgium launches investigation
articles.content_orig:
Dozens of supermarkets in Europe have reported temperatures of their refrigerators and fridges rising overnight, now widely believed to be caused by cyber attacks similar to the one that affected France several weeks ago.
Supermarket chains in Belgium, Sweden, Estonia, Netherlands, Luxembourg and Ireland have been affected.
The story began with Belgian media reporting on Monday that fridges were turned up to 17 degrees Celsius, forcing many stores to throw away food.
Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity (CCB) told Belgian outlet Belga that it is aware of an incident targeting supermarket refrigeration systems.
CCB spokesperson Katrien Eggers told Euronews Next, "We are aware of an incident, but have no further information." There are no reports yet as to who was behind the attack... and it may never be possible to identify them."
Belgium's federal prosecutor's office have opened an investigation into the incident, according to a spokesperson.
Some 40 Delhaize Proxy supermarkets, 15 Carrefour Shop & Go stores, 15 Intermarché shops and five Spar Q8 service station locations have reportedly been impacted in Belgium, according to Belgian outlet Le Soir .
Butchery group De Laet en Van Haver also said that their fridges were affected. IKEA have also said their Bergen shop located at Mons was affected, bringing the total to 75 stores affected in Belgium.
"We have identified an IT incident affecting the refrigeration systems in several dozen stores. We immediately took the necessary measures to keep our stores operational," a spokesperson from Delhaize told Euronews Next.
Carrefour told Euronews Next this morning that "the impact at Carrefour is very limited: currently 15 of our 700 stores are affected, both in Flanders and Wallonia. Not a single hypermarket is among them."
"All stores remain open because it only concerns a few refrigeration units, mainly freezers. Quick action was taken so that all stores can stay open," they added.
Meanwhile later this morning Carrefour Belgium spokesman Mich Vergauwen said, "It's a cyberattack, there is no other reason," adding that the "impact is very limited".
It's believed the incident took place between Sunday night and Monday morning, skyrocketing refrigerator temperatures.
Stephan Moelans, CEO of refrigeration installer Sabcobel, which manages Delhaize's fridges and freeze systems, told the Belga news outlet that the Belgian attack involves exactly the same mechanism as the previous French cyberattack.
"Over the past few weeks, we've been working very hard to protect our customers' fridges against this vulnerability," Moelans said.
He said the incident happened when the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode.
The refrigeration executive said a software update alone is not enough to address the vulnerability, with physical modifications required instead.
"That requires investment. The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France."
Sabcobel know of around twenty affected units, out of the hundreds it manages across Belgium.
Danfoss, the company that supplied the software for the refrigeration systems affected in both the latest incident and the one in France in October, said customers who had not updated their software were affected.
A spokesperson told VTM NIEUWS that "the company says that the vulnerability lies primarily in outdated software and that they had already urged customers to start using their new software".
Problems reportedly also occurred at a number of stores of the Swedish supermarket chains ICA and Coop last night, with refrigerators and freezers turned up to 50 degrees Celsius.
A similar incident occurred in Estonian at one location of supermarket chain Selver, according to media reports.
13 SuperValu stores in Ireland were affected by a suspected cyber incident, according to a statement by owner Musgrave made to the Irish Times.
In the Netherlands, the freezing and cooling systems of at least seventeen companies were attacked last night, according to a spokesperson for supplier Danfoss. The identities of the companies were not disclosed.
Delhaize also suspended its ordering systems in Luxembourg as a precaution to prevent a similar incident.
Finnish media report that several K Group supermarkets have been affected. K Group is one of Finland's largest retail chains.
These reported incidents follow a similar attack in France just weeks ago, on 12 October, when hundreds of French supermarkets belonging to the Intermarché and Coopérative U chains fell victim to a cyberattack targeting their refrigeration systems.

articles.title_orig: Stealth Classic Thief: The Dark Project Returns for a PS5 Remaster with New Content
articles.title_zh: Stealth Classic Thief: The Dark Project Returns for a PS5 Remaster with New Content
articles.content_orig:
One of the classics that helped create an entire genre, stealth masterpiece Thief: The Dark Project is coming to PS5 in remastered form next month, from 3rd December 2026.
This new version of the 1998 game has been remastered using Nightdive Studios' KEX Engine to produce a new edition running at 4K and 120 frames-per-second. It's got all the content of the base game, the three extra missions from Thief: Gold, and an entirely new campaign in the form of The Tarnished Mirror.
The Tarnished Mirror is a narrative bridge between The Dark Project and Thief 2: The Metal Age . In it, "a seemingly straightforward theft spirals into imprisonment, uneasy alliances and a descent into a drowned, R’lyeh-like necropolis. Players will experience an expanded enemy roster, ambitious level design and a pure Thief experience that descends into unsettling, otherworldly horror."
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
The bonus campaign has been created by the same people who made Thief: The Black Parade , which was a mod / expansion for Thief: Gold, made by the fans. "This collaboration marks a rare industry moment, with Nightdive and Eidos-Montréal welcoming a community creation directly into official canon," the press release added.
You can also expect the following from the remastered package:
Pre-orders are live on the PS Store for the PS5 digital versions, with a standard edition costing £24.99 / $29.99 and a Digital Deluxe Edition priced at £28.99 / $34.99.
In terms of physical editions, you're looking at three versions to choose from: standard, steelbook, and deluxe trapezoid. The first two are self-explanatory, but the Deluxe Trapezoid edition includes the game, steelbook, booklet, a box, and a physical remaster diary for £49.99 / $69.99:
Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.
This looks amazing. Big fan of Thief Gold so this package looks like the best it’s ever been.
I'm going to make that trapezoid box fit on the shelf. I've heard nothing but good things about that game and to see a Developer Diary (physical) included with any game is a real rarity. I'm seeing less and less context/text in art-books now. That steelbook is nice too. I'm not sure what sleeves included means, but to see them credit the illustrator too is such a good move, Clear River Games clearly know what they are doing.
Please help my wallet! Another day one for me.... Keep 'em coming.
I tried it the gog version of theif recently imon my steam deck its enjoyable but damm its hard but maybe im just bad lol i got to the level with the gambling den and havent played it since but maube i will get the remaster and give it a proper playthrough.
Very excited for this and unlike recent Nightdive remasters I think this is easily worth the £25. Will be grabbing day one and hope this is the start of even more immersive sim remasters from them!
@GirlVersusGame I’ve seen you post about your collections of stuff before and at the risk of triggering a new obsession have you looked into big box PC games of the 90s? There’s a good history of the guy who designed that box alongside some of his creations in this article.
https://obscuritory.com/essay/incredible-boxes-of-hock-wah-yeo/
Well worth a read and even has a concept mock up he did for the PS2 game cases that went unused.
If make doesn't follow the re, no sale.
More developers should collaborate with fans, similar to what happened with Sonic Mania.
@Glassneedles So actually I kind of have, I saw a big box with Robocop on it and it included a poster and the game was on a cassette. I'm realistically never going to play it but there was a poster too and how do you say no to that. It was Ocean Software, I haven't looked into many others. I want to leave limited copies of games to the genuine fans. What's happening at the moment with the jailbreak situation is affecting the resale market for PS2 games, the discs are needed so prices are jumping all over the place and those who are there for the nostalgia and the love of Retro are the ones having to pay those higher prices. I like reading books about the history of the industry too but it's mainly been console only.
I saw this too (it ended a couple of days ago) https://www.backerkit.com/c/projects/official-thief-pulse-of-promise/thief-pulse-of-promise-graphic-novel-collectibles
That Limited Celldweller Signed Picture Disc Vinyl is beautiful. They did a track for the backer project.
Companies tried to make the most eye catching boxes on the market with the PC release of Prince of Persia coming in a well remembered one.
I think there was a fair few games in the 90s (Thief, your isometric RPGs like Nox, Lands of Lore, Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights etc), I may have been too young to really appreciate...Absolute credit then to Night Dive bringing some of these old classics back into the spotlight 🙂

articles.title_orig: Mark Gurman: Apple Initially Aimed to Release iPhone Duo in November
articles.title_zh: Mark Gurman: Apple Initially Aimed to Release iPhone Duo in November
articles.content_orig:
Over the weekend, the video calling app Zoom was updated with iPhone Duo optimization. On the device's large inner display, users can now see shared content such as the host's desktop and other participants on a call at the same time.
In addition, four Microsoft apps were updated with iPhone Duo optimization today: Word , PowerPoint , Excel , and OneNote . Microsoft Outlook was already optimized for the device since it launched, but Microsoft Teams has yet to be.
Apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later are fully optimized for iPhone Duo. These apps extend to fill the entire outer and inner displays on the device, with toolbars and tab bars appearing vertically below the status bar.
Apps built with the iOS 26 SDK or earlier run on iPhone Duo, but they appear in the center of the inner display, leaving lots of empty space .
In the App Store, optimized apps have a "Made for iPhone Duo" label on the device.

articles.title_orig: Spain train crash: US, Japan and Canada citizens among dead, authorities say
articles.title_zh: Spain train crash: US, Japan and Canada citizens among dead, authorities say
articles.content_orig:
An award-winning University of Cambridge researcher died in the Spanish train disaster while on her way to collect a prize for scientific excellence.
Dr Marta Shahbazi was travelling to an awards ceremony on Wednesday when the train she was on crashed into another near Urda, south of Madrid, killing 69 people.
The mother of two was an affiliate associate professor leading a group of researchers at MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge and had earned several awards for work on human embryos and cell biology.
In a statement, the LMB paid tribute to the "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist" and described her death as a "profound shock and a huge loss".
The expert in cell biology ran the Shahbazi Laboratory at the LMB, based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus.
She had been announced as the winner of a Spanish Society for Developmental Biology award for her contributions to the study of early human development and  was due to collect the award at a conference in El Rompido in Andalusia.
The LMB said: "As a wife and mother of two young children, Marta wrote eloquently about balancing her family and career, serving as a much-admired role model for a 'mother scientist', a term she used to describe herself.
"Marta was an inspiring, talented and passionate scientist whose research shed light on the earliest steps in the development of human embryos and how errors occur that lead to failed pregnancies," the LMB said.
The institute said her death was "a profound shock and a huge loss for LMB".
Her work had been recognised with "many awards and prizes", the laboratory added.
Shahbazi is listed on the University of Cambridge website as a principal investigator at its Stem Cell Institute (CSCI).
Institute director Prof Bertie Gottgens said its community was "shocked and deeply saddened" by her death.
"Marta led her primary research group at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) alongside her roles as an affiliate principal investigator and affiliate assistant professor at the CSCI," he said.
"Across both institutes, she was highly respected for her pioneering research on early human development and valued for her collaborative spirit.
"Her creativity, passion, and generosity will be greatly missed."
The news of her death was first confirmed in a social media post by the CiMUS, based in Santiago de Compostela where Shahbazi's aunt works.
Shahbazi undertook her PhD at the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre, before joining the University of Cambridge as a post-doctoral fellow and then the LMB in 2020.
The crash in Spain happened when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of a stationary train operated by the Iryo company.
It is one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history, and Spain's worst crash since 2013.
Three days of national mourning were declared in the country.
More than 540 people were on board both trains.

articles.title_orig: Honda Africa Twin range gets bigger engine, fresh technology, and brand-new model lines
articles.title_zh: Honda Africa Twin range gets bigger engine, fresh technology, and brand-new model lines
articles.content_orig:
Honda have announced major changes to their Africa Twin adventure bike family for 2027, confirming new models, plus a capacity jump from 1084cc to 1131cc across the line-up.
Now known as the CRF1150L, the range will consist of a standard base model, plus the road-focussed Adventure Sports (AS) as before. A new off-road centric Enduro Sports will also join the brigade, with a raised front mudguard and spoked 21in front wheel.
Starting with the Adventure Sports, the base version will be joined by a new top of the line CRF1150L Africa Twin Adventure Sports Honda Sensing Ride – fitted with front and rear radar to compete against the likes of the new Triumph Tiger 1200 , and fully-specced BMW R1300GS .
Exclusively available with Honda’s semi-automatic Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT) system, the Sensing Ride is joined by two standard CRF1150L AS variants – one with a conventional manual gearbox and another with DCT in place.
All three are expected in UK dealers from March and put out a claimed 117.3bhp at 7500rpm and 87.8lb.ft of torque at 5750rpm, with the updated parallel-twin motor housed in a revised steel frame which – combined with an aluminium swingarm – cuts a claimed 1.4kg over the outgoing structure.
That’s not to say the bikes are lightweights though – far from it – with kerb weights starting at 245kg for the conventional manual, raising to 255kg for the AS with DCT. The Sensing Ride version tips the scales at 256kg – with all three getting 220mm of ground clearance and an adjustable seat height of between 830-850mm.
All three are fed by a 24.2-litre fuel tank, with Honda promising 55.4mpg for the manual version and 52.3mpg for the semi-automatic flavours. This fuel tank runs under the seat, which Honda says helps contribute to a greater mass centralisation of weight – helping the bikes to feel less top heavy and potentially more composed on the go.
This is combined with a re-positioned battery, ECU, fuel filler cap, and airbox – with Honda also keen to make life easier when manoeuvring at low speeds, especially handy when loaded up with luggage and/or a pillion passenger .
Being the road-biased version, all three roll on a 19in front and 18in rear spoked wheel, shod with a choice of Bridgestone Battlax Adventure A41s, or Michelin Anakee Roads.
Not only this, but the riding position has also been tweaked, with the handlebars now 10mm narrower and 10mm higher and further forward. The footpegs are also 10mm further forward and 20mm narrower, too.
Away from the numbers, the Africa Twins are now even cleverer than before, with Honda promising six standard riding modes that can all be personalised to the rider’s preferences. There’s also an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) for lean-sensitive rider modes, and backlit switchgear that’s said to be less complex than the current design.
The Sensing Ride takes this further with front and rear radar guidance – a first for the Africa Twin – unlocking rider support including blind spot detection, adaptive cruise control, and group ride assistance.
Alongside this, you’ll also find front and rearward collision warnings, plus ‘Distance Assist’ (to stop you getting too close to the vehicle in front on a manual throttle), and an ‘Emergency Brake Assist’ that applies some stopping power when there is a collision risk up front.
Being the clutchless DCT variant, it also gets ‘Stop & Go’, which lets the bike follow the vehicle in front during stop start traffic – a similar set-up to the semi-automatic KTM 1390 Super Adventure S Evo , launched for the beginning of 2026.
It doesn’t end there either because the Adventure Sports trio come on Showa electronic suspension as standard, known as Electronically Equipped Ride Adjustment (or EERA for short).
Working through a monoshock and chunky 49mm upside down front forks (up from 45mm), it is combined with Honda Skyhook control that continuously monitors the position of the bike to adjust damping forces in a bid improve handling, stability, and ride quality.
The EERA system itself takes data from sources including the ECU, IMU and fork stroke sensor to adjust damping by the millisecond – with 210mm of travel available at the front end, and 200mm available at the rear.
As is the way with many modern adventure bikes, a ‘Minimum’ mode will also lower the seat height by 5mm for a flatter foot and remains selected even after you’ve switched off the bike.
There’s also a raft of preload settings too, consisting of ‘Solo’, ‘Solo with Luggage’, ‘Pillion’, and ‘Pillion with Full Luggage’. Adjustment can then be further fine-tuned, including 24-steps of preload – with further electronic interventions including hill hold control, and electronically combined ABS that monitors brake pressure in the calipers at both ends for smoother applications.
Alongside the Adventure Sports comes a new CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports model, which shares many of the same creature comforts, but comes based around the updated standard model.
Promising a 9kg weight reduction, it’s distinguish it from its siblings by a pointed front beak, and HRC-style paint – however performance still comes from the same new 1131cc parallel-twin engine, meaning an identical 117.3bhp at 7500rpm and 87.8lb.ft of torque at 5750rpm.
Just like the standard model, it rolls on a 21in front and 18in spoked rim with tubeless Metzeler Karoo Street tyres, and shares the same steel frame, aluminium swingarm, riding position, electronics, and updated seven inch TFT display (with additional 5.7in screen) – with a choice of manual or DCT gearboxes available to order.
Keyless ignition, cruise control, and handguards come as standard – as do six customisable riding modes, plus an adjustable seat height of between 870mm and 890mm plus a kerb weight of 228kg for the manual and 239kg for the DCT.
Like the Adventure Sports, you’ll find CarPlay and Android Auto, with the bike receiving a higher 260mm of ground clearance and fully-adjustable 49mm closed-cartridge forks inspired by the brand’s CRF450 Rally competition bike.
Suspension comes via Showa at both ends, with 240mm of travel up front and 230mm at the rear. This works with sizeable 310mm floating wavey front discs, plus an advanced array of lean-sensitive electronics including seven stage Honda Selectable Torque Control (or traction control) which meters the amount of intervention on the throttle on- or off-road, depending on inputs from the six-axis IMU.
Other features include wheelie control, and traction can be switched off altogether if required. Unlike the Adventure Sports, the fuel capacity drops to 18.8 litres, thanks to an altered dual-tank design – however the same overall adventure bike silhouette remains.
Although still sitting at the lower end of the big adventure bike power figures, Honda’s Africa Twin motor has undergone some significant development for 2027.
For starters, there’s a redesigned intake system, plus larger-diameter 52mm throttle bodies (up from 46mm), and a revised valvetrain and cylinder head – with Honda promising an increased compression ratio from 10.5:1 to now 12.1:1.
The pistons have also changed, as have the con rods, crankshaft and balancer shafts – with options for both a six-speed manual or semi-automatic Dual Clutch Transmission system (that both share the same crankcase design).
Honda have brought the Africa Twin right up-to-date with these changes, however the fresh engine is still lacking the performance figures of some its premium big-capacity rivals. Whether you need all that punch is debatable, but the fresh electronics and revised riding position should make it a strong contender whether you fancy a trip across Europe by road, or by trail.
News Editor, trackday fan, lover of 90s sportsbikes

articles.title_orig: Wall Street's Fear Index is doing something strange. Here's what it means for stocks
articles.title_zh: Wall Street's Fear Index is doing something strange. Here's what it means for stocks
articles.content_orig:
Stocks wrapped their worst week since June on Friday, but a group of the most sophisticated options analysts agree the reaction in the options market was oddly calm.
While the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) , often referred to as a so-called fear index, did touch its highest intraday level since April on Friday, it quickly retreated and closed at 19.4. Its rollover came even as the S&P 500 finished the day down nearly 2%. For that size of a decline in stocks, the 2.2-point move in VIX was "relatively muted," according to SpotGamma's Brent Kochuba, whose analysis suggests VIX should have jumped closer to 2.6 points, based on a study of 126 selloffs since 2018.
Even in the Nasdaq 100 Index , where implied volatility increased for most options contracts, there were key exceptions. Prices on put contracts that are between 20% and 50% out-of-the-money were higher on a volatility basis after the sell-off on Oct. 16, according to data shared by Nasdaq's Kevin Davitt.
So not only did traders not pile into S&P 500 Index options on Friday, they were also especially choosy with which Nasdaq hedges they bought. For example, in the Nasdaq, puts were more expensive two weeks ago, according to Nations Indexes data. And out-of-the-money S&P 500 Index puts "just aren't being chased-into at this moment," writes Nomura managing director Charlie McElligott, indicating investor calm in the face of falling stocks.
"Index options skew hasn't been particularly reactive to the few days of spot equities selloff this week, and even where it has, it's partially a function of call vol getting mushed," McElligot said in a note to clients on Friday.
One explanation for the lack of hedging could be that asset managers are quickly selling stocks instead of using options to protect those stocks from further decline.
One popular chart making the rounds over the weekend came from Morgan Stanley's prime brokerage. According to the firm's data on long-short active managers, total global gross equity exposure is down 8% from its most recent peak, the biggest drawdown in at least ten years.
"Long/short has experienced a massive de-levering event," said Zed Francis, CIO of Chicago-based Convexitas. "Buy the shorts, sell the longs. If you were closer to cash than you were before, no need to hedge. I believe this is the main reason implied volatility has remained quiet during an increased-stress month."

articles.title_orig: Suspected cyberattacks trigger supermarket fridge failures across Europe
articles.title_zh: Suspected cyberattacks trigger supermarket fridge failures across Europe
articles.content_orig:
Suspected cyberattacks have triggered temperatures to rise in grocery store refrigeration systems in a growing number of countries across Europe.
Overnight temperature spikes were recorded in stores in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg and Sweden. On Monday, retailers and authorities pointed to alleged cyberattacks that underscored the vulnerability of systems that once largely operated mechanically.
The head of ⁠⁠⁠⁠Sweden’s national cybersecurity centre, John Billow, confirmed on Monday to the Reuters news agency that the centre ⁠⁠⁠⁠is responding to ⁠⁠⁠⁠multiple incidents affecting store cooling systems.
“We have in recent weeks … identified that we have quite a lot of exposed operational technology devices in Sweden that we have been clear about the necessity to update or patch,” he said.
The temperature of freezers in several Swedish stores rose suddenly overnight, store operators ICA and Coop said, while Swedish retailer Axfood said freezers at a distribution centre for home delivery of groceries in the Gothenburg area were hacked.
SuperValu, Ireland’s third-largest supermarket chain, ⁠⁠⁠⁠said a specific model of refrigeration systems has been affected by a “cyber incident” at 13 of its 223 ⁠⁠⁠⁠stores.
The Belga news agency reported overnight temperature increases at dozens of ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Ahold Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg. They were blamed on a cyberattack, according to the chief ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠executive ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠of refrigeration company,⁠ ⁠⁠⁠Sabcobel.
Stephan Moelans said the units’ evaporators were switched to defrost mode.
Also in Belgium, five Spar shops had their fridge systems attacked, said a spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates the franchise system.
In Estonia, at least one supermarket chain was affected, technology supplier Kitman Coldtech told public broadcaster ERR.
“This is very fresh, it happened this morning,” Kitman’s CEO Jann Mutso said, without naming the affected chain.
Ahold Delhaize reported a cybersecurity incident to Dutch police last month.
The cyberattack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets in France raised the temperature of fridges and freezers to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122F), spoiling food and causing fires at several stores.
One Swedish store said in a social media post on Monday that the temperature of its refrigerators and freezers had been set to the same temperature as during the cyberattack in France.
“We are aware that a limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems,” a spokesperson for privately held ICA told Reuters in an email.
Kitman’s Mutso also said that temperatures at the Estonian chain were set to 50 degrees Celsius (122F).
Privately-held retailer Coop told Swedish daily Aftonbladet that six of its stores had been affected by similar incidents.
There has been no claim of responsibility for Monday’s attack, nor the one earlier in France.
However, the incidents help to increase concern regarding hybrid warfare stemming from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the Iran-United States war.
European states have blamed Moscow for a growing number of incidents affecting infrastructure, including via cyberattacks, in recent months. Russia has repeatedly denied involvement in any sabotage or hybrid warfare operations.
European Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Christophe Hansen said the attacks were “a deliberate attempt ⁠to disrupt” EU food supplies and undermine public ‌confidence.
“These incidents show that cyberattacks ⁠can disrupt services, affect ⁠businesses and directly affect citizens’ ⁠daily lives”, a ⁠European Commission spokesperson ⁠said, stressing the importance of strengthening ‌cybersecurity across the bloc.
A spokesperson for The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium told Al Jazeera that the rising number of cyberattack incidents, especially those resulting from the targeted use of AI, is an evolving trend.
However, they added, “we may never be able to identify … who is behind this attack”.

articles.title_orig: Englishman Karl Bushby returns home after 28 years walking 30,000 miles around the world
articles.title_zh: Englishman Karl Bushby returns home after 28 years walking 30,000 miles around the world
articles.content_orig:
A British adventurer has completed a 28-year walking journey around the world, arriving at his childhood home after travelling some 50,000km (31,070 miles) across jungles, frozen seas and international borders.
Karl Bushby, 57, was embraced by his mother, Angela, outside her terraced house in Hull, northern England, on Monday, beneath a banner reading “Welcome Home Son”.
Hundreds of cheering supporters had welcomed him in the city centre before he made the final stretch home.
“Sorry to keep you waiting,” he joked to the crowd. “Is that it, is it done?”
Bushby began what became known as his Goliath Expedition in Punta Arenas, southern Chile, in November 1998, carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a cheap plastic camera.
His goal was to reach his home city by an unbroken route, without using motorised transport to advance his journey.
The route took him north through the Americas, across the ice of the Bering Strait from Alaska to Russia, and onwards through Mongolia and China. He later swam across the Caspian Sea before continuing towards Europe.
Along the way, he negotiated the dense jungle of the Darien Gap between Colombia and Panama, was detained after entering Russia, and faced repeated visa and funding problems.
The global financial crisis in 2008 cost him major sponsors, adding to delays that stretched what he had expected to be a 12-year journey into 28 years.
Last month, he finally swam across the English Channel, clearing the last major obstacle before beginning the final walk home.
“They say it takes a village, but literally it took a world to get me here,” he said as he arrived in Hull. “The kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation-states, to get me back here today. I didn’t do this alone. There was a big team. The biggest team. Earth.”
A feature-length documentary about his journey is in production, while Bushby plans to begin a speaking tour around England in the coming weeks.

articles.title_orig: Where things stand on Iran after tense weekend as its delegation has left Qatar
articles.title_zh: Where things stand on Iran after tense weekend as its delegation has left Qatar
articles.content_orig:
Tehran, Iran – Iran’s military is warning that if all-out war breaks out again with the United States and Israel, it will be longer and more costly than their rivals expect.
Iran’s armed forces could deploy new weapons and tactics against the US, Israel and other countries, which would be the third major conflict between the countries since June last year.
There have been increasing signs that the US and Israel’s war on Iran, which began on February 28, could restart after the US midterm elections. President Donald Trump said on Sunday that the war with Iran will end “very soon one way or the other” and Tehran should agree a deal or “the hammer” will come down.
Hossein Kanani Moghaddam, a former senior IRGC commander, told Al Jazeera that despite extensive blows to the Iranian armed forces during US and Israeli strikes earlier this year, they are now in better operational shape compared with previous conflicts.
“In terms of offence, our target database has significantly expanded, the range, accuracy and warheads of our missiles have improved and our drone capabilities have increased,” he said.
New enemy assets were being identified and operations in additional geographical areas were being planned, he added. Arkaminia said that previously undisclosed capabilities and targets would be revealed – and used – if Iran is attacked again.
Commanders from Iran’s General Staff of Armed Forces, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Islamic Republic of Iran Army are reported to have recently met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei to discuss what steps will be taken if attacked again. The response will be immediate and could go beyond the West Asia region , they said.
The IRGC was “100 percent ready” to confront another attack, spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said on Sunday evening, describing “maximum deterrence” as a goal Iran would reach in the near future.
Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said the commanders would rely on “asymmetric warfare” tactics that would compensate for the superiority of US military equipment.
He added that “some weaponry was renovated and new equipment was added along with new tactics” during the brief ceasefire period that came after the June memorandum of understanding between Iran and the US.
Last month, state television showed an underground drone production line. The authorities also showcased an upgraded version of the Arash attack drone and claimed that its warhead had doubled to 100kg with improved guidance.
According to a Reuters investigation published last week, numerous military agencies linked with Iran’s defence establishment have evaded sanctions and funnelled billions into military imports to replenish the IRGC. The imports between January 2025 and June this year from China, Russia and Germany to fuel missile and drone production included rocket propellants, explosives, detonators, titanium and heavy-duty trucks that could be used as launchers.
Many Iranian missile defence systems, radars and other equipment were hit during the war. But Kanani Moghaddam said remaining and newly developed systems were becoming more accurate, pointing to the targeting of a US-built F-35 and other warplanes and drones as successes that can be replicated and expanded upon.
“At sea, we have shown that we can easily target supertankers,” he said regarding transit through the Strait of Hormuz that is deemed “unauthorised” by Iranian authorities. He said Iranian attacks on US Navy vessels in September prompted them to stop venturing into the critical waterway since. But the US has continued its naval blockade on southern Iranian ports, while Iran’s civilian population and infrastructure remain largely exposed if the war resumes.
Tehran and other cities across the country lack shelters or early warning systems to protect civilians. Authorities have not reported any progress regarding the promised shelters and gaps in public warning arrangements.
Iran’s electricity grid, as well as oil and gas facilities, petrochemical and steel manufacturers and roads and railways could also be attacked again, making life even more difficult amid the economic crisis.
During both wars, many senior political and military figures of the Islamic Republic were killed by US and Israeli strikes.
The new supreme leader has not been seen or heard from since replacing his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in early March, ostensibly for security reasons.
This has led to tighter domestic security controls, and prompted some voices from within the establishment to raise concerns and demand accountability for intelligence failures and protection of leadership.
“We have been hit and hit hard,” state-linked analyst Hamzeh Rahim Safavi said during a televised debate on Saturday. “The main cause is intelligence weakness, but no one talks about it or is held accountable”.
The analyst is the son of Yahya Rahim Safavi, a former commander-in-chief of the IRGC who currently serves as a senior military adviser to the supreme leader. The analyst said calls by hardliners to acquire a nuclear bomb would not repair intelligence and security weaknesses.
But Esmaeil Kowsari, a former IRGC division commander now a parliamentary national-security commission member, told local media last week that even though the supreme leader and others were assassinated, “the enemies did not reach their main goals”. He said the goals were to overthrow the Islamic Republic and fragment Iran.
“On the eve of their elections, the Americans are trying to pretend that they have achieved victory by causing a ruckus and launching psychological operations, but that is not the truth,” Kowsari said.

articles.title_orig: Goodbye to the toilet brush: the more hygienic alternative more and more bathrooms are switching to
articles.title_zh: Goodbye to the toilet brush: the more hygienic alternative more and more bathrooms are switching to
articles.content_orig:
TheCoolist is a mood board for your headspace.
It sits next to every toilet, usually in a closed holder, and a Finnish cleaning expert says many people keep it far too long. In Scandinavia and Central Europe, home sites report that many households are now swapping the classic bristle toilet brush for a different design. Here’s what is replacing it, why cleaning pros say it’s more hygienic, and what it still can’t do.
According to the Norwegian site Dagens.no , many people are choosing a silicone brush over the traditional plastic one. The reasons it gives: there are no dense bristles for dirt to collect in, so the head rinses clean; the flexible head reaches the edges and hard-to-access areas; it tends to spray less; and it is often sold with a ventilated or wall-mounted holder that lets it dry faster. The site quotes Finnish cleaning expert Mari Breilin, who says plastic brushes should be replaced considerably more often than many people do. The price, it adds, is about the same as many ordinary brushes.
The British testing site Expert Reviews sums it up: bristles are “so tightly packed together that it’s impossible to clean them perfectly,” so “bacteria build-up on the brush is inevitable,” and they “need replacing much more often.” Cleaning expert Isabella Flores, of Sparkly Maid San Diego, told Tom’s Guide that silicone is non-porous, so it doesn’t absorb bacteria and organic matter the way plastic bristles can. It also dries faster and tolerates harsher disinfection, including boiling.
Silicone or not, the routine is what keeps it hygienic. Tom’s Guide recommends:
Silicone is not a miracle. Expert Reviews notes that silicone brushes shaped like regular ones “usually have weak bristles that don’t do a great job on stubborn dirt,” and that flat, spatula-style heads handle grime better, though you have to get used to a different technique. And no brush, silicone or bristle, is built to dissolve the hard mineral ring at the waterline. And whatever you choose, a brush kept damp in a closed holder will still breed bacteria.
For that waterline ring, here’s the best way to remove limescale from the toilet . The bathroom is changing in other ways too, like the option replacing toilet paper , and the floor around the base deserves attention: see why people are spraying vinegar around the toilet .
A flat silicone head, an open holder and a date to replace it. That’s the trick.

articles.title_orig: China polysilicon prices hold amid market standoff, spot-futures gap
articles.title_zh: China polysilicon prices hold amid market standoff, spot-futures gap
articles.content_orig:
The China Mono Premium, the OPIS assessment for mono-grade polysilicon used in n-type ingot production, was unchanged at CNY 38.786 ($5.82)/kg, or CNY 0.081/W, according to the OPIS Global Solar Markets Report released on Oct. 27.
According to market participants, the fundamentals of the Chinese polysilicon market remain unchanged, with the market continuing to be characterized by manufacturers holding firm to full-cost-based offers while downstream buyers show limited willingness to accept current prices. This has kept prices largely at a standstill, with inventory levels exceeding 500,000 metric tons (MT) further prolonging the impasse.
Industry participants widely noted that futures prices, which remain significantly below mainstream spot prices, have provided a degree of balance to the ongoing standoff between upstream suppliers and downstream buyers. According to data from the Guangzhou Futures Exchange on Oct. 26, settlement prices for polysilicon futures contracts for delivery between November 2026 and October 2027 ranged from a low of CNY 33.620/kg to a high of CNY 37.180/kg, with even the highest about 4.14% below the latest spot assessment.
Market participants explained that actual spot transactions continue to be concluded at higher prices than futures contracts, partly because customers with long-term purchase agreements still need to procure some material in the spot market. To offset the higher procurement costs, these buyers also source relatively lower-priced polysilicon from futures traders, helping to balance their overall purchasing costs.
One trade participant said that futures traders had been gradually selling off previously accumulated stocks of low-priced polysilicon into the spot market. However, the availability of this lower-priced material is expected to diminish over time. The participant added that manufacturers adhering to the industry self-discipline agreement appear determined not to sell polysilicon at prices below CNY 40/kg during the fourth quarter. As low-priced supplies dwindle and manufacturers maintain their price stance, futures prices are expected to gradually rise, allowing actual spot transaction prices to find a new balance between futures prices and prevailing spot offers.
Separately, an industry source said the China Photovoltaic Industry Association would organize monitoring activities to oversee the implementation of polysilicon production cuts planned for the fourth quarter, adding that this gives the market a degree of confidence and expectation that prices will remain stable. However, no official confirmation or disclosure regarding these activities was available at the time of reporting.
Looking ahead, an upstream participant expected mainstream polysilicon offers to remain unchanged until the Lunar New Year in early February 2027. Meanwhile, prices offered by manufacturers that have not signed the pricing self-discipline agreement, along with polysilicon futures prices, are expected to remain below mainstream spot offers.
The Global Polysilicon Marker (GPM), the benchmark for polysilicon produced outside China, was assessed at $19.234/kg, or $0.040/W, unchanged from the previous week.
Both manufacturers and buyers in the global polysilicon market continued to face mounting pressure. One trade participant noted that some suppliers had reduced their China-based polysilicon sales teams to just a handful of people, underscoring the increasingly weak demand environment.
On the demand side, a source at an integrated manufacturer said that certain long-term contract holders with cell manufacturing facilities in the U.S. could still absorb around 300 MT of global polysilicon per month. While this volume provides some support for demand, the contribution remains relatively small and limited in scope.
Certain long-term contract holders, despite being in poor financial condition, reportedly continue to purchase global polysilicon at a loss due to their contractual obligations. However, the pricing mechanisms embedded in long-term contracts negotiated several years ago have given buyers some room to negotiate, potentially allowing these agreements to remain in effect despite challenging market conditions.
In the near term, industry participants generally expect the main sources of global polysilicon supply to remain U.S.-produced material and lower-priced polysilicon from other origins. In addition, the framework established under the Section 232 outcome has enabled limited volumes of compliant Chinese polysilicon to continue flowing into Southeast Asia.
OPIS, a Dow Jones company, provides energy prices, news, data, and analysis on gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, LPG/NGL, coal, metals, and chemicals, as well as renewable fuels and environmental commodities. It acquired pricing data assets from Singapore Solar Exchange in 2022 and now publishes the OPIS APAC Solar Weekly Report .

articles.title_orig: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs
articles.title_zh: Government making up China policy as it goes along, say MPs
articles.content_orig:
By SAM MERRIMAN, POLITICAL CORRESPONDENT
Published: 20:12 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 22:07 EDT, 1 November 2026
Ministers have been accused of jeopardising national security by prioritising 'diplomatic politeness' with China .
A report from MPs today criticises Labour's approach to Beijing as the 'worst of both worlds'.
In a devastating indictment of its dealings with the communist state, the chairman of the business, innovation, science and trade committee (Bist) said the 'Government keeps making up its China policy as it goes along'.
Firms have missed out on lucrative commercial deals as Britain has been left increasingly exposed to 'unquantified, unmanaged risk', the report adds.
Last night the committee put pressure on the Prime Minister to clarify his stance on closer dealings with the Chinese Communist Party.
'We await confirmation of how much continuity there is between the approaches to China of the Starmer and Burnham governments,' the MPs said.
Last year Labour, under Sir Keir Starmer, refused to publish a Government review of relations with China, releasing only a short summary and arguing that publishing the full findings could damage British interests.
In June, two men were convicted of running 'shadow policing' operations on British soil, spying on Chinese dissidents and MPs who supported them.
Labour ministers have been accused of jeopardising national security by prioritising 'diplomatic politeness' with China. Pictured: PM Andy Burnham, then Mayor of Manchester, with China's Consul General Tang Rui on April 17, 2026
Labour's Ed Miliband shakes hands with Wang Hongzhi, head of China's National Energy Administration, at the China-UK Energy Dialogue in Beijing, China on March 17, 2025
Labour was accused of pandering to China after plans for a new mega embassy on the old Royal Mint site were approved in January, despite spying fears. Pictured: A concept grapohic for the proposed embassy
Labour was accused of pandering to China after plans for a new mega embassy on the old Royal Mint site near the Tower of London were approved in January, despite spying fears.
Shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat has described the report as 'damning' and accused Labour of overseeing a dereliction of its duty to the public.
He told the Daily Mail: 'Labour are distracted and allowing Beijing to dictate terms, risking economic dependence on a hostile China. This is unacceptable. The Government's disjointed, last-minute approach leaves Britain weak and susceptible to Chinese control.'
The report warns that 'low-cost, increasingly sophisticated Chinese-connected technology has proliferated in the UK' and says the Government should create a register of high-risk firms to combat the threat associated with this.
It concludes: 'We are disappointed that, in failing to create a register of high-risk jurisdictions, the Government has prioritised diplomatic politeness over the UK's national security.' However, the Government last night rejected the Bist committee report and said it 'disagrees with its conclusion'.
The committee found that Labour has re-engaged with Beijing 'without establishing the rules of the game'.
Its chairman, Labour MP Liam Byrne, said: 'Businesses cannot plan for the future when the Government keeps making up its China policy as it goes along. Ministers promised clarity and consistency.
'Instead, we have opportunities missed, risks unmanaged and decisions left until the eleventh hour. Britain must shape its own relationship with China, or risk having that relationship shaped for us in Washington or Beijing.'
China's President Xi Jinping, right, and Britain's then Prime Minister Keir Starmer, left, shake hands before their meeting at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on January 29, 2026
Bill Yuen, 65, (l) and Peter Wai, 41, (r) were convicted in June following a trial at the Old Bailey. Wai was found guilty of running a Chinese 'state intelligence service' on British soil while working as a UK Border Force officer, on the orders of former Hong Kong superintendent Yuen
The report also found products made with slave labour by repressed Uyghur Muslims ending up on British shelves. Pictured: Buildings north of Kashgar in China's northwestern Xinjiang region believed to be a re-education camp where mostly Muslim ethnic minorities are detained
Should Britain risk national security for economic ties and diplomatic relations with China?
Mr Byrne added that 'we should welcome trade that builds Britain's strength' but cease dealings that 'put that strength at risk'.
The committee recognised that disengaging from China is neither realistic nor desirable as annual trade with Beijing is now £140billion a year – about 7 per cent of total UK trade.
However it added that changes need to be made as the Government's decision-making on China – such as the takeover of British Steel from the firm's Chinese owners at a cost of £1.3million a day – has been characterised by 'reactivity, inconsistency, and opacity'.
MPs also raised concerns about the increasing adoption of cheap Chinese electric cars. These devices pose a risk to national security through spying and the ability to control vehicles remotely is a 'potential risk to life', the report adds.
The report is also damning on the risk of products made with slave labour by repressed Uyghur Muslims in the Xinjiang region ending up on British shelves.
In order to reset Britain's relationship with China, MPs have called on the Government to 'insist on fair trade' to create a 'level playing field'. Ministers should also 'prevent the transfer of sensitive technologies and data to China'.
A Government spokesman said: 'Our approach to China is consistent – we will co-operate where we can and challenge where we must.
'Our Trade Strategy makes clear that we will capitalise on every opportunity to grow our economy while never compromising on national security. Increased discussions with China allow us to directly raise concerns where they arise.'
DAILY MAIL COMMENT: It's time to drop the 'diplomatic politeness' and change your tune on China, PM...

articles.title_orig: Iranians have left Doha talks, draft proposal for US deal being circulated, official says
articles.title_zh: Iranians have left Doha talks, draft proposal for US deal being circulated, official says
articles.content_orig:
US President Donald Trump said Washington had not “finished off” Iran because Tehran wanted to keep talking, while suggesting the United States might eventually take further action.
In an interview with Miranda Devine on the Pod Force One podcast, released Monday, Trump said: “We’ve been nice because we haven’t finished them off because, you know, they wanted to talk and they keep talking, talking, talking. At some point, we’ll have to do that.”
He added that Iran wanted to make a deal, but said, “We’ll see about a deal.”
Trump also said the United States could not allow Iran to have nuclear weapons.
Russia’s foreign ministry said on Monday that reports of new military action against Iran were a cause for extreme concern.
Moscow called for greater diplomatic efforts to normalize the situation in the region.
The United Arab Emirates will be better prepared than before for whatever follows in the US-Israeli war with Iran, Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazrouei said on Monday.
Speaking at the Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference, he said the course of the war was unpredictable.
At certain points, he added, the UAE’s exports had performed better than before the war.
Iran’s position on defending its national security, sovereignty and territorial integrity has not changed, and Tehran will make no compromises on those issues, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said on Monday after meeting China’s foreign minister in Beijing.
Ali Bagheri Kani also described the killing of former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei by the United States and Israel as a “war crime.”
The spokesman for Iran parliament’s national security committee warned on Monday that a renewed war could spread geographically and strike areas not previously considered targets.
Hassan Ghashghavi said there were places “perhaps no one has thought about so far,” but said he would not discuss details.
He said Iran’s offensive and defensive capabilities had improved since the 12-day war and that a new conflict would bring “more surprises.”
Ghashghavi said an order by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei for an immediate and effective response to threats, without geographical limits, had been issued for implementation and should not remain at the level of analysis and commentary.
The gold, jewelry, silver and coin dealers’ union in Iran’s northeastern city of Mashhad has banned the sale and display of gold products featuring designs associated with the Pahlavi era or the Lion and Sun, according to an official notice to businesses in the sector.
The union said businesses found displaying or selling the items would face action.
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday that parties to the Middle East conflict should pursue political solutions rather than resume fighting, during a meeting in Beijing with Iranian national security official Ali Bagheri Kani, China’s Xinhua news agency reported.
Wang also said China supports Iran in safeguarding its sovereignty and security.
Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday, but not because of difficulties in talks aimed at ending the US-Israeli war on Iran, Reuters reported on Monday, citing an official briefed on the discussions.
A draft proposal was being circulated for feedback, and a follow-up meeting was possible, the official added.
Iran should extend its missile range beyond 2,000 kilometers and reconsider its nuclear doctrine, including developing the capability to build nuclear weapons, a lawmaker said on Monday.
Mohammad Motamedizadeh said Israel was “at the tip of our blade” and that Iran should also target “the heart of America.” He said Iran could target adversaries’ interests in the United States and Europe if threatened.
He added that there was no reason for Iran to remain in the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
He also described Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei’s remarks about responding to threats “at any level” as a sign of a shift in Iran’s nuclear posture.
